items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: But they would listen to my wife, Cecelia

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you a question. Tell us a little bit about your group, The Loud Minority.

Ah, The Loud Minority. Undisciplined, unbridled passion, and rage — happy rage. That was the most undisciplined group of men and women. I had two ladies in and out of that band — and instrumentalists, not vocalists. I had male and female vocalists, but lady instrumentalists — Janice Robinson the trombonist, and Sharon Freeman, a French horn and pianist. But we were characterized by our inability to play soft, or for lorng. I didn’t plan it that way it just happened. And everybody was a soloist. We didn’t omit…
That’s the first time I heard it put like that, Foss.
